subject: Milva McDonald City Council Candidacy
overview: John Petrella interviewed City Council candidate Milva McDonald regarding her platform and her experience as chair of the Medford Charter Study Committee. McDonald detailed her positions on ward representation, zoning overhaul, and strategies for expanding the city's commercial tax base.

items.title: Introduction and Candidate Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Milva McDonald, who discussed her three-decade residency in Medford and her professional background in journalism, education, and the arts.

items.title: Charter Study Committee Overview
items.summary: McDonald described her work chairing the committee that prepared Medford’s charter review, emphasizing the public engagement process and collaboration with the Collins Center.

items.title: Ward Representation and Governance Compromise
items.summary: McDonald discussed the committee's recommendation for ward representation and the resulting compromise between the Mayor and City Council to keep the proposal on the upcoming ballot.

items.title: Zoning Reform and Residential Impacts
items.summary: McDonald expressed support for a citywide zoning overhaul while advocating for a cautious approach to residential changes to protect neighborhoods from teardowns.

items.title: Economic Development and Revenue Generation
items.summary: Proposals for expanding the tax base included incentivizing commercial development, reviewing fee schedules, and renegotiating the pilot program with Tufts University.

items.title: Community Platform and Policy Proposals
items.summary: McDonald outlined support for affordable housing land trusts, residential tax exemptions, climate resiliency benchmarks, and the creation of an LGBTQ+ commission and a city arts coordinator.

items.title: Campaign Outreach and Closing
items.summary: McDonald shared details for upcoming campaign events at a local venue and provided contact information for voters to reach her directly.
